goals.title: Investigate the incident and record supported work

findings.summary: Regional aggregate: 26 of 402 IAD /v1/exports returned 504 during 09:45-10:00 UTC, versus 0 of 388 in ORD over the same window.
findings.detail: From gateway aggregate rows timestamped 2026-09-18T10:04:00Z: iad /v1/exports, status 504, note 26_of_402_requests_in_09:45_to_10:00_UTC (~6.5%); ord /v1/exports, status 504, note 0_of_388_requests_in_09:45_to_10:00_UTC. This is the only quantitative scope evidence and shows the problem concentrated in IAD while ORD exports succeeded in the same window.

findings.summary: Failed requests gw-084 and gw-093 have no application span in the trace export, but only about 10% of /v1/exports were sampled, so the absence is inconclusive.
findings.detail: Telemetry check at 10:06 UTC showed application spans sampled for approximately 10% of /v1/exports requests. Neither gw-084 nor gw-093 has a corresponding application span. Per the source, this absence does not show whether either request failed before reaching the application or whether its spans were simply not sampled. No failed request in the bundle has a correlated gateway, application, and database trace.

findings.summary: Hypothesis: the failing export requests may stall before reaching the application, or their application spans were simply not sampled. (inconclusive)
findings.detail: Stated as a hypothesis, not fact. The absence of application spans for gw-084 and gw-093 is consistent with a pre-application stall, but also fully consistent with the ~10% sampling rate. Would be resolved by capturing full (100%) traces for failed export request IDs and checking for app spans. Not currently supported either way.

findings.summary: Symptom: customers in region IAD receive gateway timeouts when creating /v1/exports, while ordinary dashboard reads succeed.
findings.detail: Impact: export creation (POST /v1/exports) returns a timeout instead of a downloadable report. Affected surface: Atlas Reports API, region iad only as observed. Start: earliest observed failure attempt 09:44 UTC (tenant northstar reported two attempts, 09:44 and 09:47). Latest observed failure: tenant willow attempt at 09:54 UTC; aggregate failure window extends 09:45-10:00 UTC. Scope: IAD-region export creation. Ordinary dashboard/report-list reads worked for the same reporters. Support received no reports from other regions by 10:02, but that is a count of reports, not evidence that other regions had zero failures. No cause is asserted here.

findings.summary: Hypothesis: elevated IAD database latency is contributing to the /v1/exports timeouts. (not established)
findings.detail: Stated as a hypothesis, not fact. Supporting: IAD-only DB p95 elevation (140 -> 1090 -> 980 ms) coincides in time and region with IAD-only export 504s; the one sampled success (gw-101) spent 420 ms in DB. Against/limitation: the observed p95 is about 1 s, far below the 30000 ms gateway timeout, so a p95 of this size cannot by itself explain 30 s stalls, and the DB metric is all-routes_aggregate rather than export-specific. Would be confirmed by export-route-specific DB metrics or correlated traces showing near-30 s database time on failed requests (or connection-pool exhaustion). Would be refuted if failed exports show normal DB latency and stall elsewhere (or if failures occur before the application).

findings.summary: Conclusion: the cause of the IAD /v1/exports timeouts is not established by the available evidence.
findings.detail: The evidence supports only that failures are IAD-scoped and time-coincident with a ~7x IAD database p95 elevation; there is no correlated gateway+application+database trace for any failed request, and the missing spans are uninformative at ~10% sampling. Unknowns: (1) whether failures occur inside the application or before it; (2) export-route-specific database latency, p99, and connection-pool state; (3) whether the 30000 ms stalls are caused by DB, connection saturation, or another upstream dependency. Resolving test: enable full sampling / capture correlated traces for failed /v1/exports request IDs and obtain export-specific database and pool metrics for IAD 09:40-10:00 UTC. No cause is asserted as fact.

findings.summary: Two sampled IAD /v1/exports requests returned HTTP 504 at the 30000 ms gateway timeout with gateway_note upstream_response_timeout.
findings.detail: Observed in gateway request sample: gw-084 at 2026-09-18T09:46:08Z, iad, /v1/exports, status 504, duration_ms 30000, note upstream_response_timeout; gw-093 at 2026-09-18T09:51:24Z, iad, /v1/exports, status 504, duration_ms 30000, note upstream_response_timeout. The 30000 ms matches a gateway upstream timeout, i.e. the upstream did not respond in time. These are a small sample, not the full failure set.

findings.summary: A sampled successful IAD export (gw-101, 09:55:06Z) spent 420 ms in its database query and completed in 1460 ms.
findings.detail: Trace export notes one sampled successful IAD export at 09:55 (gw-101) spent 420 ms in its database query and completed in 1460 ms. This is a success case during the incident window; it does not by itself characterize the failing requests.

findings.summary: IAD all-routes database query p95 rose from 140 ms to about 1000 ms during the incident window, while ORD stayed at 155 ms.
findings.detail: Database metric rows: iad db_query_p95_ms = 140 for 09:30-09:40, 1090 for 09:40-09:50, 980 for 09:50-10:00; ord db_query_p95_ms = 155 for 09:50-10:00. Each row is noted all_routes_aggregate, so it is not specific to /v1/exports and does not isolate export queries. The elevation is roughly 7x on a p95 basis.

findingEvidence.note: Gateway data confirms IAD-only export 504s and ORD success.
Shows IAD-only 504s matching the 30s gateway timeout.
No correlated trace for any failure; sampling gap.
Only one sampled success; no failed-request DB trace to correlate.
IAD-only DB p95 elevation, but magnitude (~1s) below timeout.

decisions.summary: Proposed interim mitigation (pending root cause): make IAD export creation resilient to slow upstreams (bounded retry/backoff and/or async job + polling) to reduce customer-visible 504s.
decisions.rationale: Failures are a minority (26/402, ~6.5%) and IAD-scoped; an async/queue or bounded-retry pattern could reduce customer-visible timeouts while diagnosis continues. This is speculative about root cause and is PROPOSED only; it requires explicit incident-lead approval and should not be applied without it.

decisions.summary: Proposed: for the next shift, acquire correlated end-to-end evidence on IAD /v1/exports failures (100% tracing + export-specific DB/pool metrics) before selecting any remediation; change no production system without incident-lead approval.
decisions.rationale: The cause is not established and there is no correlated gateway+application+database trace for any failed export; the DB p95 elevation (~1 s) is far below the 30 s timeout and is all-routes aggregate, so it cannot alone justify a targeted fix. Acting before narrowing the cause risks masking the fault. This decision is PROPOSED and has not been approved by any authorized actor.

decisionCitations.note: Cause is not established; no correlated trace for any failure.
Missing app spans are inconclusive at ~10% sampling.
Symptom is IAD-scoped export timeouts with dashboard reads unaffected.
DB p95 elevation is all-routes aggregate and ~1s, far below the 30s timeout.
Failure rate ~6.5% in IAD, 0 in ORD.

tasks.title: Pull export-specific DB latency, p99, and connection-pool metrics for IAD 09:40-10:00
tasks.description: Current DB data is all-routes_aggregate p95 only. Obtain /v1/exports-specific query latency, p99 (not just p95), and database connection-pool saturation/waits for iad across 09:40-10:00 UTC to test whether DB latency can account for the 30000 ms stalls.

tasks.title: Capture correlated traces for failed IAD /v1/exports requests
tasks.description: Enable 100% sampling (or otherwise capture application spans) for /v1/exports in IAD and obtain correlated gateway+application+database traces for the failed request IDs (gw-084, gw-093, and any others from the 09:45-10:00 window). Determine whether failures occur inside the application or before it. Resolves hypothesis find_59e9cd2eb5cd4c9a and find_4228073accd84466.

tasks.title: Confirm tenant retry outcomes and check other regions for unreported export failures
tasks.description: Support has not confirmed whether northstar/willow retries succeeded, and the 'no reports from other regions' at 10:02 is a report count, not failure evidence. Confirm retry outcomes and query gateway/app data for /v1/exports 504s in regions other than IAD over 09:30-10:30 UTC.

tasks.title: Obtain incident-lead approval before any production change
tasks.description: Both decisions on record (dec_82ef0d50fb394a8a, dec_44cd603a30a54b97) are proposals only. No remediation, timeout change, retry change, or deployment may proceed until an authorized incident lead explicitly approves a specific decision and it is accepted with a reason. Do not self-approve.
